blocks.prompt: 18. The first term of an A.P. is \(a\), the second term is \(b\) and the last term is \(c\). Show that the sum of A.P. is \(\frac{(b + c - 2a)(c + a)}{2(b - a)}\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof with letters. We know the first term, the second term and the last term.
The sum needs the number of terms \(n\), which is not given.
Plan: \(d = b - a\); find \(n\) from the last term; then use \(S_n = \frac{n}{2}(a_1 + a_n)\).
steps:
Given: \(a_1 = a\), \(a_2 = b\), last term \(a_n = c\) (with \(b \ne a\)).
To prove: \(S_n = \dfrac{(b + c - 2a)(c + a)}{2(b - a)}\).
Method: The first two terms give \(d\). The last-term formula \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) gives \(n\). Then \(S_n = \frac{n}{2}(a_1 + a_n)\) uses the first and last terms, \(a\) and \(c\).

Common difference
\[d = a_2 - a_1 = b - a\]
Why: \(d\) = second term − first term.

Number of terms
\[c = a + (n - 1)(b - a)\]
\[n - 1 = \dfrac{c - a}{b - a}\]
\[n = \dfrac{c - a}{b - a} + 1\]
\[= \dfrac{c - a + b - a}{b - a}\]
\[= \dfrac{b + c - 2a}{b - a}\]
Why: The last term is the \(n\)th term; write \(1 = \frac{b - a}{b - a}\) to add the fractions.

Sum of the A.P.
\[S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(a_1 + a_n)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{b + c - 2a}{b - a} \cdot (a + c)\]
\[= \dfrac{(b + c - 2a)(c + a)}{2(b - a)}\]
Why: Put \(n\), \(a_1 = a\) and \(a_n = c\) into the formula; \(a + c = c + a\).

Check with numbers
Take \(a = 1,\ b = 4,\ c = 13\): the A.P. is \(1, 4, 7, 10, 13\).
\[1 + 4 + 7 + 10 + 13 = 35\]
\[\dfrac{(4 + 13 - 2)(13 + 1)}{2(4 - 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{15 \times 14}{6} = 35 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The formula gives the same sum as adding directly.
